    Data: Li, X., Zhou, Y., Zhao, M. & Zhao, X., "Harmonization of DMSP and VIIRS nighttime light data from 1992–2024 at the global scale", figshare v10 (CC BY 4.0); method in Scientific Data 7, 168 (2020). Brightness is a 0–63 "digital number" (DN) per ~1 km pixel, averaged here into 0.2° cells (~20 km) inside the People's Republic of China incl. Hong Kong and Macau. "Lit" means DN above 7. 1992–2013 come from the DMSP satellites; 2014 onwards are VIIRS data converted to look like DMSP, which reads lower in its first years, so the 2014–2016 dip is a sensor change, not less light.
